title: SMOKE must drive the real entry point, not a synthetic fixture

facts.note: Needs an observer that knows the test (or the plan/acceptance/WMBT specifying it) is in the SMOKE phase, e.g. SMOKE-tagged acceptance or test id.
Task/plan text mentions planning, writing or fixing SMOKE tests or the launch path.
SMOKE test files themselves, and planner artifacts that specify SMOKE tests.
Diff-level observer for SMOKE tests being written or modified (not just planned).
Detector for banned fixtures (FakeMultiplexer, Popen of cat/sleep/python -c, _SYNTHETIC_AGENT) used as primary wiring in a SMOKE test.

fires: A SMOKE acceptance/WMBT or plan specifies a test that drives a fake multiplexer or a subprocess stub instead of the real CLI entry point.
A SMOKE-phase test is written or modified so it launches Popen(['python','-c',...]) or an embedded synthetic agent script as the agent command.
An existing SMOKE test proves the launch path only via Popen(['cat',...]) or Popen(['sleep',...]).
doesNotFire: Unit or integration (non-SMOKE) tests that use a fake multiplexer or subprocess stub to isolate a component.
A SMOKE test that drives the real CLI entry point (spawn, coach, or rendered launch prompt) and writes agent scripts to temporary files.
A SMOKE test carrying a valid, unexpired dated inline suppression for this rule.

given: A SMOKE-phase test of the agent launch / production wiring is planned (plan, acceptance, WMBT), written or modified.
when: Choosing what the SMOKE test drives as its primary production wiring.
then: The SMOKE test must drive the real CLI entry point (spawn, coach, or the rendered launch prompt), not a synthetic subprocess stub or fake multiplexer.
prefer: Run the real CLI as a subprocess (subprocess.run([sys.executable, -m, atdd.cli, spawn, ...])) or use invoke_atdd_spawn, driving the real cmux-native launch path.
Write agent scripts to tmp_path files.
avoid: FakeMultiplexer as SMOKE wiring (bypasses real surface dispatch).
Popen of cat, sleep or python -c as the agent command (pty wrapper / lifecycle only / bypasses adapter command construction).
Agent scripts embedded as string constants (e.g. _SYNTHETIC_AGENT).
Treating a green SMOKE suite as proof when it only proves the harness.
unless: Inline '# atdd:suppress(planner.smoke.synthetic-fixture-bypass) UNTIL=YYYY-MM-DD'; the debt expires on that date.
why: A stubbed SMOKE test proves the harness, not the product, and is green precisely where real wiring is untested. Incident #854: a Popen crash (missing shell=True on the adapter command tuple) stayed invisible because SMOKE used a Python stub.
evidence: SMOKE test invokes the real CLI entry point (atdd spawn / atdd coach / rendered launch prompt) or invoke_atdd_spawn, exercising real adapter command construction and the cmux-native launch path.
No banned fixture (FakeMultiplexer, Popen(['cat'|'sleep'|'python','-c',...]), _SYNTHETIC_AGENT) appears as primary wiring in SMOKE tests, unless under an unexpired dated suppression.
Agent scripts are written to tmp_path files rather than embedded as string constants.
verifier_detail: Banned fixtures in SMOKE-phase tests: FakeMultiplexer (bypasses real surface dispatch); Popen(['cat',...]) (exercises the pty wrapper, not the agent command); Popen(['sleep',...]) (proves process lifecycle, not agent behaviour); Popen(['python','-c',...]) (bypasses adapter command construction); _SYNTHETIC_AGENT (embedded script constant replacing the real adapter command).

Real entry points: atdd spawn, atdd coach, and the rendered launch prompt — the surfaces that exercise real adapter command construction and the cmux-native launch path. Accepted forms include subprocess.run([sys.executable, -m, atdd.cli, spawn, ...]) and the invoke_atdd_spawn helper.
Suppression: inline '# atdd:suppress(planner.smoke.synthetic-fixture-bypass) UNTIL=YYYY-MM-DD'; dated so the debt expires — expired suppressions do not suppress.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires/doesNotFire situations (incl. non-SMOKE unit/integration tests not firing; planning as well as writing/modifying SMOKE tests).
additions.justification: Schema requires observable activation; derived from the source's SMOKE-phase scope and banned-fixture list. Planning context added because the audience is the planner; the obligation itself stays on the SMOKE test.
